p|panel|reglas_titulo: Rules: what is blocked and what is allowed
p|panel|reglas_lead: No rule exists unless you create it. Every block records who decided it and when. Undoing never deletes: it records that it was undone.
p|panel|reglas_inviolables: Broad rules wait and respect the essentials: a whole category, the whole home or Guard Mode block nothing until GUARDIANA has watched for 24 hours, and a category or Guard Mode never touch system updates, certificates, the system’s own security and connectivity checks, time, recognized messaging and video calls, or what GUARDIANA needs for its license. One name you pick is blocked from the first minute (for the whole home, once that day is over); if it is one of those essentials, or the device has been watched for less than a day, you are asked first.
p|panel|reglas_nueva_lead: Block or allow an exact name, a family of names (the domain and everything under it) or a whole category, for one device or for the whole home.
p|panel|reglas_ninguna: There are no rules. GUARDIANA only watches.
p|panel|leyenda_desconocido: “Local network” is the devices of your home finding each other: it does not go out to the internet. “Delivery” is a network that carries other companies’ content: not the destination, the road. “Its site”, “your account”, “its server”, “content”, “settings”, “measurement”… is what the name itself says (www, login, api, cdn, config, analytics…): a hint, not a check. “Service” is a name of a known company that no list marks and whose name does not say what it is for. “Unclassified” means that no public list knows it, and neither does our company list; not that it is suspicious. “Sport”, “news”, “banking”… is what a well-known website does, from our open list of sectors.
p|panel|leyenda_colores: The three colors of the category. Green: normal, what a service needs to work (its website, its server, your account, updates, content, your home network). Orange: worth a look; it measures what you do, serves ads or nobody knows it (advertising, telemetry, measurement, ads, unclassified). Red: alert; a public list recognizes it as tracking, the company is registered as a data broker, or it tries to evade monitoring. It is a way of reading the category, not a verdict: click the label to learn what it means, and allow or block each row with its switch.
p|panel|cat_enlace_guia: Click to learn what it means
p|panel|alcance_cortar_todo: It applies to the whole device, not only to the agent: the block is by name, for any program. On Windows, if the system says so, GUARDIANA tells you afterwards which program asked, but it cannot block just one.

p|panel|alcance_cortar_off: Off. GUARDIANA records what falls outside the job, but blocks nothing.
p|panel|alcance_cortar_on: On. While the AI works, it only reaches what is on the list. Everything else is blocked and shows up here for you to decide.
p|panel|alcance_cortado_aviso: Blocking here stops the next attempt. It does not undo what was already sent, and it does not reach an agent that does not use GUARDIANA as its DNS.

p|panel|regla_esperado_prohibido: That cannot be blocked by category: it is system updates, certificates, the system’s own security and connectivity checks, time, recognized messaging and video calls, and what GUARDIANA needs for its license. If you really want to block one of those names, create a rule with that exact name.

p|panel|modo_bloqueo_lead: When GUARDIANA blocks a name, by default it answers “that name does not exist” (NXDOMAIN). The other option is to answer with an empty address (0.0.0.0). Applied when GUARDIANA restarts.
p|panel|mi_reglas_lead: The rules of this device: the ones you created from here, which you can undo here, and the ones the home panel set for it, which only change there. The home panel does not see the detail of what you ask unless you share it with the box above.
p|panel|verify_lead: The same thing guardiana verify prints: facts, not promises. If something does not add up, it shows here.
p|panel|verify_limite: The signature and the public record only make sense for released versions. How to check by hand, without trusting the program: docs/VERIFY.md in the repository.
p|panel|licencia_lead: One program, two levels. The first 7 days you have everything, without paying. After that, without a license, GUARDIANA does not switch off: it moves to GUARDIANA Free, for good, and keeps watching this computer (the live globe, which program talks to which country, company and category, your own blocks and the last 24 hours), with the DNS as it is. With Plus (a monthly or yearly subscription, or Lifetime, paid once) you get everything else: the whole history, several devices, alerts, automatic blocks, reports and ZERO. What was written down always stays on your disk.
p|panel|licencia_prueba: Trial: {d} days left (ends on {fecha}). Nothing is charged; when it ends GUARDIANA moves to Free and keeps watching this computer.
p|panel|licencia_prueba_uno: Trial: 1 day left (ends on {fecha}). Nothing is charged; when it ends GUARDIANA moves to Free and keeps watching this computer.
p|panel|licencia_prueba_texto: The seven days are counted on your computer, in two places: your ledger and a separate mark that only an administrator can remove ({donde}). That mark holds the date they started and the latest time the program has seen, so setting the clock back does not stretch the trial. Nothing else. We say so here because we hide nothing we do on your computer.
p|panel|licencia_prueba_sin_marca: The seven days are counted on your computer, in your ledger. The separate mark that stops them from starting over ({donde}) could not be written because GUARDIANA has no administrator rights, so for now the date is only in the ledger.
p|panel|licencia_ancla_texto: A copy of your key, of this activation’s number and of the product is also kept in {donde}, where only an administrator can touch it, so losing the data folder does not lose what you paid for. Not your name, not your email.
p|panel|licencia_ancla_sin_marca: The copy of your key that should be kept in {donde} (so losing the data folder does not lose what you paid for) could not be written: GUARDIANA has no administrator rights. For now the license lives only in your ledger.

GUARDIANA keeps watching this computer on Free; what was written down stays on your disk. If you think this is a mistake, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
p|panel|licencia_prueba_agotada: The trial ended on {fecha}. GUARDIANA keeps watching this computer on GUARDIANA Free, with the DNS as it was. What was written down is whole on your disk and you can export it. To get everything in Plus back, activate your license key.
p|panel|licencia_clave_lead: The key arrives by email when you pay. One connection to {host}, started by you, to activate it; then one check 8 days after activation and one per billing period (monthly or yearly; the Lifetime license, paid once, one a month, so that a refund reaches this computer too). If a check cannot be done (no internet, the gateway down), it is tried again every hour until it goes through. All of them are recorded in “What GUARDIANA knows about you”. Nothing else leaves your computer.

p|panel|licencia_limite: Without a license GUARDIANA does not switch off: it moves to Free and keeps watching this computer, with the DNS as it is. Cancelling deletes nothing of what was written down.
